note: Synthetic Phase 4 end-to-end personas. The same person at three difficulty levels so results are comparable. No real client content.

personas.person: Synthetic person: 57, married, partner 59. One occupational pension. Articulate, states figures plainly with correct labels.
personas.expectation: Every module-critical input is supplied clearly. The only thing the background planner has to repair is the primary age, which the live lane hears in the first sentence but does not canonicalise — the exact defect Phase 3 was built for.

turns.client: I'm 57 and I'm married. My partner is 59. I'd like to get my pension sorted out before I retire.
turns.speech: Thanks for that. Let's look at your pension together. When were you hoping to retire?
turns.comment: THE SCRIPTED DEFECT: the partner's age is canonicalised and the client's own age is not, even though they said it first. This reproduces the production failure rather than papering over it.

turns.client: I'd like to retire at 62 if the numbers work.
turns.speech: Sixty-two, noted. What is your occupational pension worth at the moment?

turns.client: The occupational pension is worth about 319,000 right now.
turns.speech: Three hundred and nineteen thousand. And what are you earning, and what goes in each month?
turns.comment: The planner reads the transcript window, finds the age the live lane missed, and repairs it. The quote must be an exact contiguous span of turn 1 or the real validator rejects it.

turns.client: I'm on 95,000 a year. I put in 6 percent and the company puts in 8 percent.
turns.speech: Ninety-five thousand, six percent from you and eight from the company. Is that pension still being paid into now?
turns.comment: The live lane refuses this figure: three numbers in one turn and no salary cue next to the 95,000, so the numeric guard fails closed with live_numeric_fact_unsupported. That refusal is the fast lane working as designed — and repairing it from the transcript afterwards is precisely what the background planner is for. This is the rejected_note trigger doing its job.

turns.client: Yes, it's still being paid into every month.
turns.speech: Good. And roughly what annual income would you want in retirement, in today's money?

turns.client: My partner has no pension of their own.
turns.speech: Understood. And what income would you want a year in retirement?
turns.comment: The opening line puts a partner on the record, so the module asks for the partner's pension too — exactly as pension_medium does. This turn was not needed while the live lane was refusing "My partner is 59"; once that age is captured, the conversation has to resolve the partner's pension the way a real one does.

turns.client: I'd want about 45,000 a year.
turns.speech: Forty-five thousand a year. Let me check where that leaves us.

personas.brief:
You are Margaret Doyle, 57, and you want your pension sorted before you retire. You are articulate and organised: you answer the question you were asked, give figures plainly and correctly labelled, and you do not wander. You volunteer the relevant number as soon as it is asked for.

The financial truth, identical in all three personas: you are 57, married, and your partner is 59. You have ONE pension, an occupational scheme worth 319,000 euro. You want to retire at 62. You earn 95,000 euro a year gross. You pay in 6 percent and your employer pays 8 percent, and it is still being paid into. You would like about 45,000 euro a year in retirement, in today's money. Your partner has no pension of their own. You have no other pensions, and no other figures beyond these. If asked anything this brief does not cover, say plainly that you do not know.

personas.person: The same synthetic person as pension_easy, phrased so the live lane captures every module-critical input itself.
personas.expectation: A CONTROL, not a scenario. pension_easy deliberately needs the background planner to close two gaps, so a failure there could belong to the reconciler or to anything downstream of it. This one needs no repair at all, which isolates confirm_and_run and deterministic module execution from the reconciler entirely. Same person, same figures, same module, same expected arithmetic.

personas.person: Margaret Doyle, 57 — the same household as pension_easy, told differently.
personas.expectation: Same financial truth, different delivery. What varies is how hard the facts are to hear, not what they are, so a difference in outcome is a difference in the lane and not in the case.
personas.brief:
You are Margaret Doyle, 57, and you want your pension sorted before you retire. You talk the way people actually talk: you answer in a roundabout way, sometimes give two things at once, and sometimes correct yourself a moment later. Twice in the conversation, give a figure slightly wrong and then correct it in a LATER turn — say 'sorry, I said 62, I meant 63 — no, 62, 62 is right' or 'actually the pension is more like 319 than 300'. Refer back to things indirectly: 'the one I mentioned', 'that figure I gave you'. Never invent a number the brief does not contain; corrections must land back on the true figure.

You earn 95,000 euro a year gross. You pay in 6 percent and your employer pays 8 percent, and it is still being paid into. You would like about 45,000 euro a year in retirement, in today's money. Your partner has no pension of their own. You have no other pensions, and no other figures beyond these. If asked anything this brief does not cover, say plainly that you do not know.
personas.opening: I'm 57 — well, 57 last month. I want to get the pension sorted before I finish up.

personas.brief:
You are Margaret Doyle, 57, and you are vague, anxious and easily sidetracked. You rarely give a clean figure first time: say 'somewhere around three hundred and twenty' before settling on the real number when pressed. Mix yourself up with your partner — say 'we' and 'our pension' when you mean yours, and let the assistant work out whose is whose. Wander off topic at least twice (the weather, whether any of this is worth doing, how your sister managed her retirement) before coming back. Express uncertainty about when you will actually retire: 'maybe 62, maybe I'll keep going, I honestly don't know' — but if pressed for the plan, 62 is the answer. Never invent a figure the brief does not contain: if you do not know, say so.

personas.opening: I suppose I'm wondering about the pension really. We're both getting on, I'm 57.

personas.person: 41, working, wants to know if the rainy-day fund is enough
personas.brief: You are 41 and still working. You have about EUR 18,000 in savings and spend about EUR 2,600 a month. You want to know whether your emergency fund is enough. Answer naturally and briefly. Do not volunteer figures you were not asked for.
personas.opening: I want to know whether the savings I have would actually cover me if something went wrong.
personas.expectation: The scalar-only module. No entity binding at all, so it isolates module-agnosticism in the harness from the entity machinery pension exercised.

turns.client: I want to know whether the savings I have would actually cover me if something went wrong.
turns.speech: That is worth knowing. Roughly how much do you have set aside, and what do you spend in a typical month?

turns.client: I have about 18,000 saved, and I spend around 2,600 a month.
turns.speech: Eighteen thousand set aside against two thousand six hundred a month. Let me check where that leaves you.

personas.person: 38, one mortgage, wants to know whether to switch
personas.brief: You are 38 with one mortgage: about EUR 240,000 left, on 4.1 percent, with 22 years to run. You want to know whether switching is worth it. Answer naturally, give figures when asked, and do not volunteer anything you were not asked about.
personas.opening: I have been wondering whether I should switch my mortgage or just leave it alone.
personas.expectation: One liability entity with three numeric slots. Proves the entity binding hardened on pensions works on a different collection.

turns.client: I am 38 and I have been wondering whether I should switch my mortgage or just leave it alone.
turns.speech: Worth checking. What is left on it, what rate are you paying, and how long is left to run?

turns.client: There is about 240,000 left, I am on 4.1 percent, and there are 22 years to go.
turns.speech: Two hundred and forty thousand at 4.1 percent over twenty-two years. Let me look at that.

personas.person: 38, one mortgage, misremembers the rate and corrects it
personas.brief: You are 38 with one mortgage: about EUR 240,000 left with 22 years to run. When first asked the interest rate say it is 4.5 percent. Two turns later, correct yourself: say you checked and it is actually 4.1 percent. Answer naturally and do not volunteer figures you were not asked for.
personas.opening: I want to know if my mortgage is costing me more than it should.
personas.expectation: The correction path OUTSIDE pensions. 4.5 must be superseded by 4.1, and supersededFigures must catch it if it is not.

personas.person: 44, one child, wants to know the cost of college
personas.brief: You are 44 with one child, a daughter aged 8. You want to know what college will cost and whether you are saving enough. You think it is around EUR 12,000 a year today. Answer naturally.
personas.opening: I would like to work out what college is going to cost for my daughter.
personas.expectation: Entity binding on the DEPENDANTS collection, which has no owner key at all - a shape pension never exercised.

personas.brief: You are 44 with two children: a daughter aged 8 and a son aged 11. You want to know what college will cost for both. You think it is about EUR 12,000 a year each in today's money. Answer naturally, and refer to them by name or age rather than repeating everything each time.
personas.opening: We are trying to work out what college will cost for the two children.
personas.expectation: MULTI-ENTITY binding where the entities are near-identical. Two children must not become three dependants, and each age must land on the right child.

personas.brief: You are 46. You own your home, worth about EUR 420,000, with about EUR 180,000 left on the mortgage. You have about EUR 25,000 in savings and a pension worth about EUR 90,000. You spend about EUR 3,200 a month. You want to see where you stand overall. Answer naturally.
personas.opening: I would like to get a clear picture of where we actually stand financially.
personas.expectation: SEVERAL collections populated in one conversation - property, liability, asset, pension. Proves they do not contaminate each other.

personas.person: 46, married, talks about everything as ours
personas.brief: You are 46 and married. Talk about your finances the way couples do - say 'our house', 'we have', 'between us'. The house is worth about EUR 420,000 and is in both your names. The mortgage of about EUR 180,000 is joint. You have about EUR 25,000 saved between you. Your own pension is worth about EUR 90,000 and it is yours alone. Your partner is 44. Answer naturally.
personas.opening: We would like to see where we stand overall, the two of us together.
personas.expectation: HOUSEHOLD LANGUAGE and joint ownership. 'Ours' must become joint ownership where it is true and must not invent a partner holding where it is not.

personas.person: 31, buying with a partner, two incomes
personas.brief: You are 31 and buying your first home with your partner, who is 30. You earn EUR 62,000 gross and your partner earns EUR 48,000 gross. You have EUR 55,000 saved between you and pay EUR 1,450 a month in rent. You are looking at houses around EUR 400,000 and spend about EUR 2,900 a month. Answer naturally.
personas.opening: We are hoping to buy our first place and want to know what we can realistically afford.
personas.expectation: JOINT INCOME attribution, which pension never meaningfully exercised: two incomes, two people, and neither may absorb the other's salary.
